claims.text: The initial material is equiatomic as-cast HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
A 50–100 nm alumina coating can be deposited on cast HfNbTaTiZr by atomic layer deposition.
The ALD alumina coating will form a continuous scale on HfNbTaTiZr.
The alumina scale will remain adherent and thermally stable at approximately 1000 °C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere for 10–50 hours.
The alumina scale acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Inhibiting oxygen diffusion into HfNbTaTiZr will suppress oxidation of the substrate.
The thin alumina coating will not alter the bulk microstructure of HfNbTaTiZr.
Coated HfNbTaTiZr will have lower oxide-scale thickness than untreated HfNbTaTiZr after exposure at 1000 °C in air.
Coated HfNbTaTiZr will have lower oxidation-associated weight gain than untreated HfNbTaTiZr after exposure at 1000 °C in air.
The coating will preserve approximately the untreated alloy's room-temperature tensile ductility after high-temperature exposure.
The coating will preserve approximately the untreated alloy's yield strength at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The predicted benefit is bounded to temperatures up to 1000 °C and exposure times of 10–50 hours.
The optimal alumina-coating thickness and its long-term adhesion under combined thermal and mechanical loading remain uncertain.
